slot: GDPR / CCPA basics for global users

pick.name: GDPR baseline kit: Common Paper DPA + sub-processor list + RoPA
pick.what: Sign DPAs as processor, publish sub-processors, keep a record of processing, honour data-subject rights
pick.why: Free and covers what B2B buyers actually ask for; EU representative only needed when processing isn't 'occasional'

alts.name: Prighter (EU/UK GDPR representative)
alts.why: Needed once you regularly process EU/UK residents' data with no EU establishment
alts.free_limits: Small tier EUR 852/yr per region (EUR 71/mo annual or EUR 79/mo monthly), EU and UK priced separately; no setup fee; no free tier

alts.name: CCPA applicability check
alts.what: California law applies only above thresholds
alts.why: Over USD 25M revenue, 100k+ CA consumers bought/sold/shared, or 50%+ revenue from selling data; a solo founder is below all three

candidates.name: Prighter
candidates.verdict: Add when EU/UK B2C usage becomes regular

decision: Art. 27 requires an EU representative unless processing is occasional, low-risk and not large-scale special-category data, so a B2C app with regular EU users eventually needs one. CCPA thresholds (USD 25M revenue / 100k consumers) exclude you for now. Respect US state-law opt-outs anyway.
details: GDPR applicability to non-EU sellers depends on targeting EU users; verify with a lawyer.

verify.note: Baseline kit is sound. Note that the CCPA USD 25M revenue threshold has been CPI-adjusted since 1 Jan 2025 (USD 26.625M, from verifier memory, not fetched); harmless here.
